Statement: The public library has installed self-checkout kiosks to make the book-issuing process faster. This indicates that the library wants to speed up the process, not necessarily to blame anyone or guarantee perfection.

Assumption I: The statement does not assume that librarians are the main cause of delays. The kiosks could be introduced to reduce waiting time regardless of who or what causes delays. Hence, this assumption is not implicit.

Assumption II: The statement does not assume perfect functioning of kiosks. It only implies that kiosks are intended to make the process faster, even if occasional malfunctions occur. Therefore, this assumption is not implicit.

So, neither Assumption I nor Assumption II is implicit.

The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Article 338B into the Constitution.

This article provides constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).

Before this amendment, NCBC was only a statutory body (created by an Act of Parliament in 1993).

Article 338

Deals with the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC).

Article 338A

Deals with the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST).

Article 340

Provides for the appointment of a commission to investigate conditions of backward classes.

Further Insights

The 102nd Amendment also inserted Article 342A related to SEBCs(Socially and Educationally Backward Classes)

NCBC now has powers similar to NCSC and NCST.

The President appoints the Chairperson of NCBC.

The Supreme Court interpreted the 102nd Amendment in the Maratha reservation case (2021).

The 105th Constitutional Amendment (2021) restored states' power to identify OBCs.

The Siddi community are descendants of East Africans who came to India through trade, , or military service centuries ago.

They are mainly settled in:

Gujarat

Karnataka

Maharashtra

Their traditional dance is called Dhamal, also known as Mashira Nritya.

The Dhamal dance is known for:

Use of animal skins and feathers in costumes

Energetic movements

Rhythmic drumming

A special drum often referred to as the Dhamal drum

The performance reflects strong African cultural roots blended with Indian traditions.

Further Insights

Siddis are recognized as a Scheduled Tribe in Gujarat.

Their culture reflects a mix of African and Indian traditions.

Dhamal is often performed during festivals and social gatherings.

Some Siddis historically served in royal armies of Indian rulers.

Their music strongly features drum-based rhythms.

In medieval Rajput tradition:

Jauhar referred to the act of mass self-immolation by Rajput women to avoid capture during enemy invasions.

Saka referred to the act where Rajput men dressed in saffron robes and fought to the death in the final battle after Jauhar was performed.

These practices were associated with Rajput ideals of honor, bravery, and sacrifice during sieges.

Bhakti and Sufism

These were religious reform movements focused on devotion and spirituality.

Mansab and Jagir

These were administrative systems of the Mughal Empire.

Mansab = military rank system.

Jagir = land revenue assignment.

Din-i-Ilahi and Sulh-i-kul

Both were associated with Emperor Akbar.

Din-i-Ilahi was a religious experiment.

Sulh-i-kul meant universal tolerance.

Further Insights

Jauhar was notably performed during the sieges of Chittorgarh.

Rani Padmini is often associated (though debated historically) with a famous Jauhar episode.

Saka warriors wore saffron (kesariya) as a symbol of sacrifice.

During the Mahajanapada period (c. 600 BCE onwards), the main source of revenue for the state was land revenue.

The standard share of produce collected from farmers was called Bhaga.

It usually amounted to one-sixth of the total produce.

Kara

Kara was a general term for tax or tribute, often paid by subjects or conquered territories.

Bali

Bali originally meant offering or tribute, sometimes voluntary in early Vedic times.

Shulka

Shulka referred to custom duties, tolls, or trade taxes.

It was collected on goods during trade and transportation.

Further Insights

The Mahajanapada period saw the rise of territorial states with organized taxation.

Magadha became powerful partly due to efficient revenue collection.

Land revenue became the backbone of early Indian state systems.

Officials were appointed to collect taxes in organized kingdoms.

The shift from tribal assemblies to monarchies increased systematic taxation.

Tex-RAMPS (Textile Sector Reforms, Assistance and Modernization for Policy Support) is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Ministry of Textiles.

In a Central Sector Scheme:

The entire funding is provided by the Central Government.

Implementation is directly overseen by the Union Ministry.

Tex-RAMPS is fully funded by the Centre (with assistance from international financial institutions like the World Bank), making it a Central Sector Scheme.

Further Insights

Tex-RAMPS aims to improve the competitiveness of the Indian textile sector.

It focuses on policy reforms and institutional strengthening.

The scheme supports research, innovation, and sustainability in textiles.

Central Sector Schemes are fully funded by the Union Government.

Centrally Sponsored Schemes require cost-sharing between Centre and States.

Villi are tiny finger-like projections present in the inner lining of the small intestine.

Their main function is to:

Increase surface area

Help in rapid absorption of digested nutrients into the bloodstream

Each villus contains:

Blood capillaries (for glucose, amino acids, etc.)

Lacteals (for absorption of fats)

To secrete bile

Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder,

To produce pancreatic juice

Pancreatic juice is produced by the pancreas,

To move food quickly

Movement of food happens due to peristalsis (muscle contractions),

Further Insights

Microvilli are even smaller projections on villi.

The small intestine is about 6 - 7 meters long in adults.

Most digestion and absorption occur in the small intestine.

Lacteals inside villi absorb fats.

Damage to villi (e.g., in celiac disease) reduces nutrient absorption.

The northern part of the Ganga - Brahmaputra delta, especially in West Bengal, is called the Moribund Delta.

"Moribund" means dying or inactive.

In this region:

River channels have shifted southward.

Water flow has reduced.

Old river courses remain.

The Upper Plains

The Active Delta

The active delta is mainly in Bangladesh, where rivers are still depositing sediments.

The Bhangar Land

Further Insights

The southern part of the delta is the active delta region.

The moribund delta has poor drainage and waterlogging.

The Hooghly River flows through the western part of the delta.

The Indian Penal Code (IPC) was drafted under the chairmanship of Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay.

He was the head of the First Law Commission of India (1834).

Although the IPC was drafted in 1837, it was officially enacted in 1860.

The IPC included provisions related to the Age of Consent, making it one of the earliest legal frameworks addressing such issues in colonial India.

Known for the Doctrine of Lapse and expansion of British territories.

Lord Bentinck

Abolished Sati in 1829.

Introduced social reforms,

Lord Curzon

Known for the Partition of Bengal (1905).

Further Insights

The IPC came into force on 1 January 1862.

It was inspired partly by English criminal law but adapted to Indian conditions.

The IPC remained in force in India until being replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (2023).

Section 375 of IPC deals with rape laws.

The Age of Consent Act was later amended in 1891 to raise the age.

The Portuguese introduced Baroque architecture, which became prominent in churches of Goa such as the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Sé Cathedral.

Baroque style is known for:

· Grand facades

· Decorative interiors

· Heavy ornamentation

· Dramatic artistic elements

"Iberian" refers to architectural traditions from the Iberian Peninsula (Spain and Portugal). Portuguese colonial architecture in Goa reflected these influences.

Gothic Revival and Indo-Saracenic

Indo-Saracenic was a British fusion style combining Indian and Islamic elements.

Neoclassical and Victorian

Both styles were introduced mainly by the British during colonial rule.

Seen in buildings like Government Houses and administrative structures.

These are European styles, but they were not the dominant architectural forms introduced by the Portuguese in India.

Palladian style became popular in Britain, not specifically in Portuguese India.

Baroque architecture emphasizes movement, grandeur, and emotional appeal.

El Niño is the warm phase of the ENSO (El Niño - Southern Oscillation) cycle.

It involves warming of surface waters in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean.

It usually weakens the Indian summer monsoon.

This can lead to below-normal rainfall and drought conditions in India.

La Niña is the cool phase of ENSO.

It generally strengthens the Indian monsoon.

It often brings above-normal rainfall.

This can sometimes lead to floods, but not lack of rainfall.

So it is not associated with extreme lack of rainfall in India.

Further Insights

ENSO stands for El Niño - Southern Oscillation.

El Niño years are often linked to global temperature rise.

La Niña can increase the chances of floods in India.

ENSO affects weather patterns worldwide, not just India.

The Southern Oscillation refers to changes in air pressure patterns across the Pacific.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. You should do this task or you will be fired by us.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

You should do this task or you will be fired by us.

options.html: This task should be done by you or we will fire you.

options.html: This task should have been done by you or we will fire you.

questions.solution:
· The correct answer is (a) This task should be done by you or we will fire you.

· The subject of the Active Voice is changed into object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed is changed into subject of the Passive Voice.

· The usage of a helping verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

· Preposition "by" is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.

· These types of questions contain Modal verbs and they should be used correctly as stated below.

· Modal verbs can be identified by the following:

o Can

o Could

o May

o Might

o Shall

o Should

o Will

o Would

o Must

o Ought to

· The format of sentences containing Modal verbs in Active voice is: Subject + Modal + V1 + Object.

· Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Subject (Objective case) + Modal + be + V3 + by + Object (Subjective case).

· For example:

o You can do this. (Active Voice)

o This can be done by you. (Passive Voice)

· The options except (a) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

· Therefore, the correct answer is: This task should be done by you or we will fire you.

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The team members _______ on the project for weeks.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The team members _______ on the project for weeks.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'have been collaborating'. "Have been collaborating" is the present perfect continuous tense, which is used to describe an action that started in the past and is still ongoing in the present. In the given sentence, it indicates that the team members started collaborating on the project in the past and are still collaborating on it.

Option (b) is grammatically incorrect. "Had collaborating" is not a valid verb form in English. The correct form is "had collaborated," which is the past perfect tense. It indicates an action completed before another past action. However, this tense is not suitable for the given sentence because it doesn't convey the ongoing nature of the collaboration.

Option (c) is incorrect because "has" is singular, but "team members" is plural. The subject and verb must agree in number.

Option (d) is grammatically incorrect because "collaborate" is in the base form of the verb, and it should be in the present participle form "collaborating" to match the tense of "have been" (the present perfect continuous tense is formed using "have been" followed by the present participle (-ing form) of the verb).

Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. Despite the initial reluctance of the management to implement the new policy, persistent employee demands eventually led to its adoption.
questions.questionHtml:

Despite the initial reluctance of the management to implement the new policy, persistent employee demands eventually led to its adoption.
questions.solution: The most appropriate antonym for the word reluctance is willingness. Reluctance means an unwillingness or hesitation to do something. In the given sentence, it refers to the management's unwillingness to implement the policy. Willingness is the opposite, meaning readiness or eagerness to do something. Hesitation refers to a pause or delay due to uncertainty, which is similar in meaning to reluctance, not the opposite. Resistance means opposition or refusal to accept something, which is also similar to reluctance. Disinclination means a lack of enthusiasm or unwillingness, making it another synonym rather than an antonym. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.solution:
'Lest' is always followed by 'should'. If you do something lest something unpleasant should happen, you do it to try to prevent the unpleasant thing from happening. So, 'would' should be replaced with 'should' to rectify the given sentence. Therefore, the error is in the segment in option (b). Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no substitution required, select 'no substitution required'. The CEO of the company (has been resigned) due to personal reasons.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no substitution required, select 'no substitution required'.

The CEO of the company (has been resigned) due to personal reasons.
questions.solution:
The original sentence is incorrect. "Has + been + ed/en verb" is a structure which is used to indicate a passive voice. The sentence should be in active voice as the subject "the CEO" is the doer of the action. Option (c) is also a passive voice structure. Option (a) will not fit in the sentence as there is no helping verb to be used before the main verb. Therefore, "had resigned" is the correct choice.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The CEO of the company (had resigned) due to personal reasons.

Note:

Voice of a sentence - Depending upon the emphasis we want to lay we use a particular voice in a particular context. We use active voice to lay emphasis on the doer of the action while we use passive voice to lay emphasis on the receiver of the action.

Example:

Active- Radha will work. (emphasis on Radha)

Passive- Work will be done by Radha. (emphasis on Work)

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence. S1. The dedicated scientist tirelessly A. advancing our understanding B. pursued answers through rigorous C. of the universe with each D. research, unravelling mysteries and S6. carefully designed experiment.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below. While the first and the last parts (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the parts in between are jumbled up. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent sentence.

S1. The dedicated scientist tirelessly

A. advancing our understanding

B. pursued answers through rigorous

C. of the universe with each

D. research, unravelling mysteries and

S6. carefully designed experiment.
questions.solution:
S1 sets the stage by introducing a dedicated scientist and his/her tireless efforts. Part B comes next, as it elaborates on the scientist's pursuit of answers, emphasizing the rigorous nature of their approach. Part D logically follows, building upon the idea of pursuit and describing the outcome of the scientist's research - unravelling mysteries. Also, 'rigorous' in part B is an adjective and would appropriately be followed by the noun 'research' in part D. So, BD is a mandatory pair. Part A comes after, highlighting the scientist's contribution to advancing our understanding of the universe. Finally, Part C provides a fitting conclusion by emphasizing the ongoing nature of the scientist's work, suggesting that with each experiment, their understanding of the universe deepens. Rearranging parts in the order of BDAC forms a coherent sentence. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The final sentence would be: The dedicated scientist tirelessly pursued answers through rigorous research, unravelling mysteries and advancing our understanding of the universe with each carefully designed experiment.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The widespread consensus on fat people is that they are lazy, ignorant gluttons who simply will not get off the couch and get on the treadmill. B. Then there's the dearth of activewear, the majority of which is not produced in plus sizes. C. The lesser-known reality is that treadmills typically have weight limits between 200 and 300 pounds, as do many bikes, stair-climbers, and other common gym types of equipment. D. questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The widespread consensus on fat people is that they are lazy, ignorant gluttons who simply will not get off the couch and get on the treadmill.

B. Then there's the dearth of activewear, the majority of which is not produced in plus sizes.

C. The lesser-known reality is that treadmills typically have weight limits between 200 and 300 pounds, as do many bikes, stair-climbers, and other common gym types of equipment.

D. Fitness is already a practice of the privileged as it requires time, money, and access that many people don't have.
questions.solution:
A is the introductory sentence as it tells us about the general perception of big individuals that they are lazy, oblivious gluttons who refuse to get off the sofa and onto the treadmill. Thereafter, C follows A as it tells us that the lesser-known fact is that treadmills, like many bikes, stair-climbers, and other common gym equipment, have weight restrictions of 200 to 300 pounds. After that B follows as it mentions that besides the fact that is mentioned in C, there's the scarcity of sportswear, which is largely unavailable in plus sizes. D is the concluding sentence as it highlights the fact that fitness has become a privileged discipline since it necessitates time, money, and access that many people lack.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (b) ACBD.
